name: Adaptive Strategy Selection

adaptive_strategy_selection.signal: No validated repeated empirical strategy evidence is available. Adaptive strategy preferences cannot yet be changed.

adaptation_rules.stable_strategy: Increase future preference only when repeated comparable empirical evidence supports stability.
adaptation_rules.declining_strategy: Decrease future preference when repeated comparable empirical evidence indicates decline.
adaptation_rules.inconsistent_strategy: Preserve uncertainty and request further testing instead of automatically promoting or rejecting.
adaptation_rules.insufficient_evidence: Keep the strategy neutral and do not alter preference.
adaptation_rules.single_result: Never modify strategy preference from a single outcome.
adaptation_rules.prediction: Never treat a prediction as an empirical outcome.
adaptation_rules.selection_score: Never treat an internal selection score as evidence of real-world strategy effectiveness.
adaptation_rules.context: Strategy adaptation remains context-sensitive. Evidence from one context must not automatically override evidence from another context.

confidence_update.reason: ACT45 adapts strategy preferences from empirical evidence but does not independently recalibrate global confidence.

cognitive_learning.capability: Adapt future strategy preferences according to validated empirical evidence about which strategies remain effective, decline, or require more testing.
cognitive_learning.what_nox_learned: Strategy selection should not remain static. When repeated empirical evidence becomes available, future strategy preferences can be adapted without confusing adaptation with execution.
cognitive_learning.future_use: Use validated strategy-performance evidence to influence future action selection while preserving context and uncertainty.

next_action: Continue collecting repeated comparable real outcomes so adaptive strategy preferences can be validated.
next_cognitive_step: ACT46 should learn to balance competing strategy preferences when several strategies are simultaneously supported, declining, or uncertain.
